title: Where the fingers hit the valves; Lee Collins and Keppard hiding his hand
summary: Punch and Allen compare finger placement, with Lee Collins's unusual overlap and Keppard hiding his hand.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: I was going to ask you about where you hold your trumpet and your fingers on the valves, what part of the fingers hits the valves? Huh? What part of your fingers hits the valves?
Right on the ball that...
That ball of your finger tip in other words.
Some people feel like that, but I feel like that.
They hold their fingers up above it some of them. Yeah some of them right? Almost straight down in other words with their fingers.

Yeah I have to do that like that. That looks clumsy. Now Lee Collin, he played just like this. I don't see how I can get his fingers out of the way. He plays right... Yeah, just like that. What part of the hand do you call that? It seems right, I don't know how he can do that. And get his hand out of the way, you know. Right all of them, right over like that.
He just overlaps it and right there in that first joint right next to your palm. Sure did. That first section of your finger there, he hits next to the palm. That's strange. Anybody else do that?
He's the only one I see do it.
They do it to some degree. A lot of trumpet players overlap to a certain degree, rather than playing on the balls and the fingers.
Well I mean, I couldn't understand. I never could play like that. I always did put my hand on the end.
Well some of them hit right along in here, about in that middle section of your fingers. A punch actually.
Lewis almost on all the lead though. He don't go for his lead. Yeah. But Lewis go about long, yeah, you know. That's where he fingers.
Towards the middle of his fingers.
Yeah, remember. He tried. I mean, he kind of hides, you know, hides some kind of where he hides.
How much pressure did they use in the old days?
I don't know. Just to tell the truth about it, I don't know, I used to wake hard.
A lot of it, huh? Yeah.
Put anything you got at it. Mm-hmm.
You talk about hiding. Freddie Kepler used to hide his hand.
Yeah. I was telling him how rough he was. Wasn't he rough with all of them? Pop, like that. That's what he used to play with.
Moose, put your name down. We want to get your name today. What is it? Manuel Joseph Zango. Moose. Moose, okay.
Ha, ha, ha, Moose. That's funny about the thing. The average musician that got something kind of funny name.
Put a little Freddie Kepler down for him. Let him hear how he kept it.
Let me see how that thing he used to play on.
That's what he used to play.
That's what he used to play. It's like that.
